about: Sales and use tax exemptions for a generating project's construction purchases, read from each state's statute, quoted. The exemption becomes the tool's default exemption for that state and technology (docs/methods/forecast.md, section 5); a state and technology not here has none read, and the tool's sales tax is before exemptions. Request numbers are rows of runs/w4/probe.csv on lab-desktop (chain 239).

land_based_wind.quote: Wind energy conversion systems, as defined in section 216C.06, subdivision 19, that are used as an electric power source are exempt, and the materials used to manufacture, install, construct, repair, or replace them are exempt.

54. a. The sales price from the sale of wind energy conversion property or hydroelectricity conversion property to be used as an electric power source and the sale of the materials used to manufacture, install, or construct wind energy conversion property or hydroelectricity conversion property used or to be used as an electric power source.

utility_pv.quote: 90. The sales price from the sale of solar energy equipment. For purposes of this subsection, "solar energy equipment" means equipment that is primarily used to collect and convert incident solar radiation into thermal, mechanical, or electrical energy or equipment that is primarily used to transform such converted solar energy to a storage point or to a point of use.
utility_pv.arithmetic: JEDI's utility PV taxable base is its materials and equipment, 0.642105 of the cost: mounting 0.105263, modules 0.368421, electrical 0.105263, inverter 0.063158. The modules (collect and convert) and the inverter (transform to a point of use) are the equipment the subsection names: (0.368421 + 0.063158) / 0.642105 = 0.672131 of the tax. Mounting and electrical materials are not named, so their tax stays.
utility_pv.ruling: Whether Iowa's solar exemption reaches racking and wiring is a reading of the statute: default, it does not (67.2 percent of the tax exempt).

utility_pv.tip: Colorado exempts components used to produce electricity from a renewable source from the state's 2.9 percent sales and use tax, not from city or county taxes unless adopted locally (C.R.S. 39-26-724): the state's part of the rate, 36.76 percent of the tax. Energy storage is not exempt.
utility_pv.quote: the exemption does not apply to any city or county sales tax administered by the Department, unless the city or county has adopted the exemption by ordinance or resolution

utility_pv.tip: New Jersey exempts solar energy devices and systems, storage of solar energy included (N.J.S.A. 54:32B-8.33): 100 percent.
utility_pv.quote: Solar Energy Devices: Solar energy devices or systems designed to provide heating or cooling, or electrical or mechanical power by collecting and transferring solar-generated energy and including mechanical or chemical devices for storing solar generated energy are exempt.

utility_pv.tip: Connecticut exempts solar electricity generating systems, their equipment and installation (2007 Conn. Pub. Acts 242, s. 68; CERT-140): 100 percent.
utility_pv.quote: This certificate may only be used for purchases exempt under 2007 Conn. Pub. Acts 242, §68.

utility_pv.tip: Kentucky treats a solar plant's generating machinery as machinery for new and expanded industry, exempt (KRS 139.480(10), KY-TAM-21-01); batteries, communication equipment and substation materials are taxable. The tool holds the modules and inverters, (0.368421 + 0.063158) / 0.642105 = 67.2 percent of JEDI's taxable purchases; mounting, trackers and DC items are exempt too, so the tax shown is an upper bound.
utility_pv.quote: Components of the commercial operation for the generation of electricity through solar power meet the definition of "manufacturing" for purposes of Kentucky sales and use taxes.
